content.title: UNC basketball head coach candidate: Tommy Lloyd
content.text: The search for a new men's head basketball coach at North Carolina is officially on. Following the firing of Hubert Davis, North Carolina is now seeking a new head man in charge, and it's a hire they really have to get right.Among the rumored list of candidates is an Arizona head coach, Tommy Lloyd. The Wildcats have been one of the best teams all season long, entering the NCAA Tournament as a No. 1 seed, and have advanced to the Elite 8 for the first time since 2015.AdvertisementFor North Carolina, Lloyd appears to be their primary target. Despite finding success at Arizona, going to Chapel Hill could be considered an upgrade for the head coach. But is he a good fit for North Carolina?Tommy Lloyd's prior experienceFeb 8, 2020; Moraga, California, USA; Gonzaga Bulldogs head coach Mark Few and assistant coach Tommy Lloyd look on during the first half against the Saint Mary's Gaels at McKeon Pavilion. Mandatory Credit: Darren Yamashita-USA TODAY SportsLloyd comes from the Mark Few coaching tree. During his playing career in JUCO, Gonzaga scouted Lloyd but didn't offer him a scholarship. Instead, they offered him a chance to get into coaching. He joined the Bulldogs as a graduate assistant in 1999 and then joined the staff full-time in 2000.Lloyd served as Gonzaga's top international recruiter under Few, getting credit for landing some big-time international prospects. After declining several interviews for jobs, Lloyd finally left and took the Arizona job in 2021.AdvertisementIn his time with Arizona, Lloyd is 147-35 overall and 6-4 in the NCAA Tournament. He's earned a few different honors, including being named the AP Coach of the Year in 2022, the Pac-12 Coach of the Year in 2022, the Sporting News Coach of the Year in 2026, and the Big 12 Coach of the Year in 2026.Why Tommy Lloyd is a good fitMar 25, 2026; San Jose, CA, USA; Arizona Wildcats head coach Tommy Lloyd smiles during a practice session ahead of the west regional of the men's 2026 NCAA Tournament at SAP Center. Mandatory Credit: Eakin Howard-Imagn ImagesOne of the keys to this is the style of play that a candidate will bring. For Lloyd, it's similar to what Tar Heels' fans are used to. Lloyd's style is to push the ball up the court and focus on rebounding. Arizona loves to play with tempo and get out and run. That fits North Carolina perfectly.AdvertisementIn terms of offensive rebounding, Arizona has been in the top 20 in the country in four of his five seasons. That would be a welcome sight for the Tar Heels, who struggled with rebounding this season.Lloyd is also a good recruiter. We told you about his international experience with Gonzaga, but he's done a good job at Arizona as well. He's coming off a year in which he had the No. 2 class in the country, headlined by Koa Peat and Brayden Burries. He also has a top-five class for next year as of right now.UNC has struggled at times in recruiting and retaining those recruits. Lloyd could fix that.The case against Tommy Lloyd at UNCMar 2, 2026; Tucson, Arizona, USA; Arizona Wildcats head coach Tommy Lloyd looks towards his players during the first half of the game against the Iowa State Cyclones at McKale Memorial Center. Mandatory Credit: Aryanna Frank-Imagn ImagesThere doesn't seem to be a lot of negatives with Lloyd and UNC in terms of a fit. He does have limited experience as a head coach with just these five seasons at Arizona. But to counter that, he was patient at Gonzaga and was a really good assistant coach with the Bulldogs.AdvertisementThe only obstacle for the program would be the buyout of $11 million, which drops to $9 million on April 1st and then the cost to get him here. Lloyd will likely command a lot of money if he's leaving Arizona.However, money shouldn't be a problem for the Tar Heels.The other question is, would Lloyd leave the west for North Carolina? Being a native of Washington, Lloyd has spent his entire life out west. He seems comfortable out there in Arizona, and we already know how families and lifestyle changes can impact things.What are the chances Tommy Lloyd ends up at North Carolina?Mar 22, 2026; San Diego, CA, USA; Arizona Wildcats head coach Tommy Lloyd reacts in the first half against the Utah State Aggies during a second round game of the men's 2026 NCAA Tournament at Viejas Arena. Mandatory Credit: Denis Poroy-Imagn ImagesLloyd appears to be the top candidate for the Tar Heels. When a blue-blood job opens up, it's an intriguing option for any coach to listen to. Landing Lloyd would be a A+ hire for the Tar Heels and would provide a lot of comfort and momentum for the program.AdvertisementIf he's at the top of the list, the Tar Heels have to find a way to land him. The question will come down to when Arizona's season ends. Lloyd won't take a job until the Wildcats are eliminated and they have already reached the Elite 8. Will UNC be patient and wait for Lloyd?I think he will be the guy regardless. It's hard to say no to North Carolina and a pay raise in the process.This article originally appeared on Tar Heels Wire: UNC Basketball: Tommy Lloyd head coach profile
